newsitem.title: USA: Gerber Products recalls baby rattles.
newsitem.headline: Gerber Products recalls baby rattles.

text.p: Gerber Products Co said on Wednesday that it will recall about 60,000 baby rattles because they pose a choking and inhalation hazard to young children.
Gerber, a unit of Swiss drug and nutrition company Sandoz AG, said the recall involves red-handled versions of the Gerber Flip Fingers Rattle, but not green-handled versions.

Spherical end caps attatched to the rattles' bright red, U-shaped handle, may separate, Gerber said, releasing small part, such as spinning plastic pieces and noise-making beads, which could present a choking hazard.
Gerber said it will offer consumers a full refund for the rattles, which were introduced in May at a retail price of $1.39 and sold in grocery stores and specialty stores.
The part number listed on the rattle's clear plastic package on a blue card is 76250.
Gerber, which made the announcement in conjunction with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, said it has received reports five of the rattles breaking, but has not heard of any injuries.

Gerber spokesman Van Hindes said the company has not yet determined whether it will introduced a new version of the red Flip Fingers rattle. Gerber, whose main business is baby food, buys the product under contract from a manufacturer in China, Hindes said.
